Battle of Chosin Reservoir: North Korea. The name "Chosin" is derived from the Japanese pronunciation "Chōshin", instead of the Korean pronunciation.

Shays's Rebellion: United States. The fighting took place in the areas around Springfield during 1786 and 1787.

Latin Empire: Old French. It existed from 1204 C.E until its disestablishment in 1261 C.E.

Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic: Belarusian. The republic was ruled by the Communist Party of Byelorussia.

Sultanate of Mogadishu: Somali. Established by Abubakr bin Fakhr ad-Din, who served as the first Sultan of the Mogadishu Sultanate and the Fakhr al-Din dynasty.

The fifth Umayyad caliph, ruling from 685 until his death in 705, this member of the first generation of born Muslims took power as Umayyad authority had collapsed across the caliphate amid civil war — name this caliph?
Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (July/August 644 or June/July 647 - 9 October 705), was the fifth Umayyad caliph, ruling from April 685 until his death in October 705.
Nicknamed the 'Knight King' or 'Soldier King' for his role in World War I, this Belgian monarch succeeded his uncle Leopold II to the throne in 1909 — who was he?
Albert I of Belgium (8 April 1875 - 17 February 1934) was King of the Belgians from 23 December 1909 until his death in 1934.
Born in the colonial Carolinas and married to Rachel Donelson, this Army general turned seventh U.S. president lent his name to a whole democratic movement — who is he?
Andrew Jackson (March 15, 1767 - June 8, 1845) was the seventh president of the United States from 1829 to 1837.
Married to Benazir Bhutto in 1987, this politician later served two separate terms as Pakistan's president, decades apart — who is he?
Asif Ali Zardari (born 26 July 1955) is a Pakistani politician who has served as the 14th president of Pakistan since 2024.
George Washington trusted this major general enough to hand him command of West Point — which he then schemed to surrender to the British in 1780. Who was the would-be turncoat?
Benedict Arnold was British military officer (1741–1801).

Active from the 1930s into the early 1950s, this British spy ring passing Soviet secrets became public in 1951 when two members suddenly fled the country — name the ring, known by its university and headcount?
Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period

Cambridge Five was a spy ring in the United Kingdom that passed information to the Soviet Union during the Second World War and the Cold War and was active from the 1930s until at least the early 1950s.
A former Unilever executive who rose to CEO of Air New Zealand, he became leader of the Opposition in 2021 and prime minister two years later — who is he?
Christopher Luxon (born 19 July 1970) is a New Zealand politician and businessman who has served as the 42nd prime minister of New Zealand since 2023.
Nicknamed the 'King of the Wild Frontier,' this American frontiersman represented Tennessee in the U.S. House of Representatives before dying while fighting in the Texas Revolution — who is he?
Davy Crockett (August 17, 1786 - March 6, 1836) was an American politician, militia officer and frontiersman.
Followers of this modern movement pick careers and donate to charities based on rigorous cost-benefit calculations, aiming to maximize positive impact worldwide — what movement is this?
Effective altruism (EA) is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good.
This former guerrilla movement, born from a 1980 merger of leftist Salvadoran factions, later became a political party after El Salvador's long civil war ended in 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front is a Salvadoran left-wing political party and former guerrilla rebel group.
Speaking a Continental Celtic language and bearing the hallmarks of La Tène culture, this Iron Age people spread across what is now France, Belgium, and beyond — who were they?
Gauls (Ancient) were a group of Celtic peoples of mainland Europe in the Iron Age and the Roman period (roughly 5th century BC to 5th century AD).

Schooled in exile in the US and Argentina after his party's founder was ousted, he came home to lead the opposition coalition against a military dictatorship — and served as Panama's president from 1989 to 1994. Who was he?
Guillermo Endara (May 12, 1936 - September 28, 2009) was a Panamanian politician who served as the president of Panama from 1989 to 1994.
Cast off Mount Olympus by his mother due to a congenital impairment, this Greek god presided over fire, metalworking, and volcanoes — who is he?
Hephaestus (eight spellings; Ancient) is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes.
Known to the Romans as Somnus, this Greek god of sleep is the namesake behind a word for an induced trance — who is he?
Hypnos (Ancient), also spelled Hypnus, is the personification of sleep.
This criminal-defence lawyer represented Bramalea—Gore—Malton in Ontario's legislature before leading a major Canadian federal party from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

Jagmeet Singh (born January 2, 1979) is a Canadian politician and lawyer who served as the leader of the New Democratic Party (NDP) from 2017 to 2025 and as the member of Parliament (MP) for Burnaby South from 2019 to 2025.

Having left school at 13 to join Melbourne's labour movement, this Labor leader served as Australia's prime minister through most of WWII's Pacific war and is often ranked among the nation's greatest — who was he?
John Curtin (8 January 1885 - 5 July 1945) was an Australian politician who served as the 14th prime minister of Australia from 1941 until his death in 1945.
This politician represents the Sircilla constituency in the Telangana Legislative Assembly and was named Most Inspirational Icon of 2015 by a major Indian broadcaster — who is he?
K. T. Rama Rao (born 24 July 1976), commonly known as KTR, is an Indian politician and Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) of Telangana Legislative Assembly.
This American politician served as South Dakota's governor before becoming the eighth U.S. secretary of homeland security in 2025 — who is she?
Kristi Noem (NOHM; ne Arnold; born November 30, 1971) is an American politician serving as the United States special envoy for the Shield of the Americas since 2026.
Before becoming the 28th U.S. secretary of defense, this retired Army general was the first African American to command U.S. Central Command — who is he?
Lloyd Austin (born August 8, 1953) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 28th United States secretary of defense, from 2021 to 2025, under the Biden administration.
Born into the House of Valois in Lorraine, this queen consort of Henry VI became a driving force of the Lancastrian cause in the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou (23 March 1430 - 25 August 1482) was Queen of England by marriage to King Henry VI from 1445 to 1461 and again from 1470 to 1471.
A poet and broadcaster who entered politics through the Labour Party, this Irishman served as mayor of Galway before becoming president of Ireland from 2011 to 2025 — who is he?
Michael D. Higgins (born 18 April 1941) is an Irish politician, poet and broadcaster who served as the president of Ireland from November 2011 to November 2025.

This Indian lawyer and Indian National Congress leader served as party president from 1919 to 1920 and again from 1928 to 1929, and fathered the man who would become independent India's first prime minister — who is he?
Motilal Nehru (6 May 1861 - 6 February 1931) was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician affiliated with the Indian National Congress.
Before becoming France's president in 2007, this Paris-born politician served as mayor of Neuilly-sur-Seine and led the UMP party — who is it?
Nicolas Sarkozy (sar-KOH-zee; born 28 January 1955) is a French former politician who served as the president of France from 2007 to 2012.

This American showman built fame on celebrated hoaxes and co-founded a legendary circus — though he insisted the cynical phrase 'there's a sucker born every minute' was wrongly pinned on him — who was he?
P. T. Barnum (July 5, 1810 - April 7, 1891) was an American showman, businessman, and politician remembered for promoting celebrated hoaxes and founding the Ringling Bros.
The fifth Roman governor of Judaea under Tiberius, he's named in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds — and is even venerated as a saint by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Who is he?
Pontius Pilate was the fifth governor of the Roman province of Judaea, serving under Emperor Tiberius from 26/27 to 36/37 AD.
Nicknamed 'electric brain' for his calm under pressure, this U.S. admiral commanded Task Force 16 at Midway, where American dive bombers sank four Japanese fleet carriers — who was he?
Raymond A. Spruance (July 3, 1886 - December 13, 1969) was a United States Navy admiral during World War II.

Sparked in 1917 amid wartime bread shortages and battlefield defeats, this upheaval abolished a monarchy and installed a socialist government after two successive uprisings and a civil war — what is it called?
Russian Revolution was a period of political and social change in Russia, starting in 1917.
This liberal, pro-European Ukrainian party takes its name from a sitcom starring the man who'd go on to become the country's real president — which party?
Servant of the People (SN) is a liberal, centrist, pro-European political party in Ukraine.
This ruler quelled a rebellion in Gdańsk and worked closely with chancellor Jan Zamoyski during his decade as king of Poland — who was he?

Stephen Báthory (27 September 1533 - 12 December 1586) was King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania as well as Prince of Transylvania (1576-1586), after previously being Voivode of Transylvania (1571-1576).
This German politician has co-chaired the far-right Alternative for Germany party since 2019 alongside Alice Weidel, and is known for pro-Russian, eurosceptic foreign-policy views. Who is he?
Tino Chrupalla (born 14 April 1975) is a German politician from the far-right party Alternative for Germany (AfD).
After heading the Soviet gas ministry, this man became Gazprom's first chairman, then Russia's Prime Minister for six years during the transition from a planned to a market economy — who is he?
Viktor Chernomyrdin (9 April 1938 - 3 November 2010) was a Soviet and Russian politician and businessman.
Praised for strategy but condemned for scorched-earth tactics against the Confederacy, this Ohio-born Union general from a politically prominent family graduated West Point in 1840 — who was he?
William Tecumseh Sherman (tih-; February 8, 1820 - February 14, 1891) was an American businessman, author, and United States Army general in the Union Army during the American Civil War (1861-1865).

After 30 years without one, France got a woman back in its top government post in May 2022—the second ever to hold it. A civil engineer and transport minister, who took the reins during a time of national transition?

Élisabeth Borne (born 18 April 1961) is a French politician who served as Prime Minister of France from May 2022 to January 2024, becoming the second woman to hold the position of Prime Minister and the first in 30 years.
This Austrian-born politician became chancellor of Germany in 1933 and took the title Führer the next year, launching the Second World War with his 1939 invasion of Poland — who was he?
Adolf Hitler: Dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945.
A five-term Italian prime minister and Christian Democracy leader, this statesman was kidnapped by the far-left Red Brigades in March 1978 — who was he?
Aldo Moro: Prime Minister of Italy (1963–1968; 1974–1976)

Fought from the 17th century to the end of the 19th, this long series of conflicts pitted European colonial powers, and later the United States, against native tribes primarily over land — what is this era of conflict known as?
American Indian Wars: Frontier conflicts in North America, 1609–1890s.

Anthony Eden: UK Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.
A poet as well as a statesman, this BJP co-founder became the first non-Congress figure to serve a full term as India's prime minister. Who is he?
Atal Bihari Vajpayee: Prime Minister of India (1996; 1998–99, 1999–2004)

Fought on July 4, 1187, between Crusader states and Saladin's Ayyubid forces, this battle removed the Crusaders' capability to wage war in the Holy Land and returned military dominance to the Muslims. It's named for a nearby extinct volcano. What is it?
Battle of Hattin: 1187 Saladin victory over the Crusaders.
This American professor co-founded the far-left Weather Underground in 1969, a group that bombed public buildings against the Vietnam War and was branded domestic terrorists by the FBI — who is he?
Bill Ayers: American professor and activist. William Charles Ayers (born December 26, 1944) is an American retired professor and former community organizer.
The only known biological son of Julius Caesar, this last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt co-ruled with his mother Cleopatra VII before his execution by Octavian — who was he?
Caesarion: Pharaoh of Egypt from 44 to 30 BC.

Founded in 1910 in Paris by its trailblazing namesake, this house ditched corseted silhouettes for functional garments and is famous for its No. 5 perfume and signature Suit — which luxury fashion house?
Chanel: French fashion house. Chanel ( shə-NEL, French: [ʃanɛl]) is a French luxury fashion house founded in 1910 by Coco Chanel in Paris.
Killed alongside Benito Mussolini by Italian partisans in April 1945, this woman was the Italian dictator's mistress — who was she?

Clara Petacci: Mistress of the Italian dictator Benito Mussolini (1912–1945). Clara "Claretta" Petacci (Italian: [klaˈretta peˈtattʃi]; 28 February 1912 – 28 April 1945) was a mistress of the Italian dictator Benito Mussolini.

A former financial analyst for Merrill Lynch subsidiaries, this Taiwanese politician became a Legislative Yuan member in 2022 and ran as Ko Wen-je's vice-presidential running mate in the 2024 Taiwanese presidential election — who is she?
Cynthia Wu: Taiwanese business executive and politician.

Believed to cause possession requiring an exorcism, this class of malevolent supernatural being has roots stretching back to the Paleolithic age and entered Jewish tradition via Zoroastrian influence during the Persian era — what is it?
Demon: Evil supernatural being. The original Ancient Greek word daimōn (δαίμων) did not carry negative connotations, as it denotes a spirit or divine power.

Before leading the commission that investigated the 1963 Kennedy assassination, which California governor became chief justice and authored the majority opinions in Brown v. Board of Education and Miranda v. Arizona?
Earl Warren: Chief Justice of the United States from 1953 to 1969.

Ranging from calls for reform to outright opposition to membership, this political stance holds that European integration undermines national sovereignty and democratic legitimacy — which position?
Euroscepticism: Body of criticism of the European Union.

Launched on 4 October 2009 by comedian Beppe Grillo and web strategist Gianroberto Casaleggio, this Italian populist party won 25.6% of the vote in the 2013 general election and is now led by Giuseppe Conte — which party?
Five Star Movement: Italian political party. The Five Star Movement (Italian: Movimento 5 Stelle [moviˈmento ˈtʃiŋkwe ˈstelle], M5S) is a political party in Italy, led by Giuseppe Conte.
The first female student at Abeokuta Grammar School, this Nigerian educator and women's-rights organizer wove together anti-imperialist, Pan-Africanist, and feminist ideals — who is she?

After his father was executed in the Stockholm Bloodbath, he led a war of liberation and was elected king in 1523 — the day Sweden left the Kalmar Union and now its National Day. Which Swedish king?
Gustav Vasa: King of Sweden from 1523 to 1560.
A founding member of Hezbollah in 1982, this Lebanese Shia cleric became its third secretary-general in 1992 and led it until his assassination in 2024 — who was he?
Hassan Nasrallah: Secretary-General of Hezbollah from 1992 to 2024. Under Nasrallah's leadership, Hezbollah acquired rockets with a longer range, which allowed them to strike at northern Israel.
Measured on 10 July 1913 at Furnace Creek Ranch in Death Valley, California, this scorching 134.1°F reading still stands as the world's hottest officially verified air mark — what is it?
Highest temperature recorded on Earth: Weather record.
Succeeding his father Babur at just 22, this second Mughal emperor lost his entire realm to a rival before reclaiming the throne shortly before his death in 1556. Who is he?
Humayun: Mughal emperor from 1530 to 1540 and from 1555 to 1556.
A conflict from 1922 to 1923 following Irish independence, fought between the Provisional Government of Ireland and the Anti-Treaty IRA over the Anglo-Irish Treaty. What is this?

Irish Civil War: 1922–1923 conflict between factions of the IRA. The National Army benefited from substantial quantities of weapons provided by the British government, particularly artillery and armoured cars.
Born in 2007 as the youngest grandchild of Queen Elizabeth II, this British royal was known by a viscount's title until 2023 and is a nephew of King Charles III — who is he?
James, Earl of Wessex: Member of the British royal family (born 2007)
At just 16, this Australian sailor spent seven months attempting a solo circumnavigation of the globe, an achievement later dramatized in the 2023 Netflix film True Spirit — who is she?
Swallowed by a great sea creature after fleeing his divine mission to warn Nineveh of God's judgment, this reluctant prophet later became known as a symbol of repentance — who was he?
Popularly known by his initials, this politician served as Telangana's first Chief Minister for nearly a decade and founded the regional party Bharat Rashtra Samithi — who is he?
K. Chandrashekar Rao: 1st chief Minister of Telangana from 2014 to 2023.

Also known as Cheops, this Fourth Dynasty pharaoh is generally credited with commissioning one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World — yet survives in just one tiny complete ivory portrait. Who was he?
Khufu: Fourth Dynasty ancient Egyptian pharaoh. Khufu, or Cheops, was the second pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning during the 26th century BC in the early Old Kingdom period.

Founded in 2016 by Jean-Luc Mélenchon, this left-wing to far-left French party pushed an eco-socialist program called 'A Shared Future' and saw its founder narrowly miss the presidential runoff in 2017 — which party?
La France Insoumise: French political party. La France Insoumise (French: [la fʁɑ̃s ɛ̃sumiz], lit. 'France Unbowed'; LFI or FI) is a left-wing to far-left political party in France.
Founded in 1988 and currently led by Ed Davey, this UK political party is the third-largest in the House of Commons with 72 MPs — what is it?
Liberal Democrats (UK): British political party. The Liberal Democrats, colloquially known as the Lib Dems, is a political party in the United Kingdom.
A member of the Fang ethnic group who began as a colonial customs agent, he became the first Prime Minister and then President of Gabon, serving until his death in 1967 — who was he?
Léon M'ba: Prime Minister (1959–61) and President (1961–67) of Gabon.

Ruling Panama from 1983 to 1989 through puppet presidents while amassing a fortune in drug trafficking, this dictator was ousted by a U.S. invasion despite past ties to American intelligence — who was he?
Manuel Noriega: Military dictator of Panama from 1983 to 1989. Born in Panama City to a poor pardo family, Noriega studied at the Chorrillos Military School in Lima and at the School of the Americas.
Serving as president of an organization that advocates overthrowing Iran's government, which Iranian dissident politician was born in December 1953?
Founder of the agrarian movement AGROunia, this politician served as Poland's deputy minister of agriculture from 2023 to 2025 — who is he?
Michał Kołodziejczak: Polish politician. Michał Kołodziejczak (born 14 September 1988) is a Polish politician and founder of AGROunia.
This former Afghan president took shelter in a UN compound in Kabul after a failed flight to India, living there until the Taliban's 1996 capture of the city ended in his assassination — who was he?
Mohammad Najibullah: Leader of Afghanistan from 1987 to 1992.
Serving as Lebanon's prime minister across three separate terms since 2005, this politician lost his final bid for a fourth term in January 2025 to the ICJ president, 9 votes to 84 — who is he?
Najib Mikati: Prime Minister of Lebanon (born 1955)
Head of the Soviet secret police at the height of the Great Purge, this Stalin-era official orchestrated mass arrests and executions before being arrested and executed himself in 1940 — who was he?
Nikolai Yezhov: NKVD director under Joseph Stalin (1895–1940)
This was the U.S. military's codename for its multinational campaign against the Islamic State across Iraq, Syria, and Libya — which campaign?
Operation Inherent Resolve: Military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant.
Born to minor Prussian nobility, he commanded the Imperial German Army in WWI and, though no friend of Nazism, as German president handed Hitler the chancellorship in 1933 — who was he?
Paul von Hindenburg: President of Germany from 1925 to 1934.
This Odawa war chief led Native Americans against the British in the Great Lakes region from 1763 to 1766, in a conflict that came to bear his name — who was he?
Pontiac (Odawa leader): 18th-century Native American war chief.

She served as France's Minister of Justice under Sarkozy before later becoming Minister of Culture across four different governments, and has been mayor of one of Paris's arrondissements since 2008. Who is this French politician?
Declared independent on a man-made platform in the Adriatic in 1968, this micronation used Esperanto as its official language before being demolished by Italian authorities — what was it called?
Republic of Rose Island: 1968 micronation in the Adriatic Sea. The Italian government viewed it as a ploy by Rosa to raise money from tourists while avoiding national taxation.
This U.S. Army officer led E Company's assault on the Belgian town of Foy after the siege of Bastogne was broken, and later served as the American governor of a Berlin prison — who is he?
Nominated by President George W. Bush in 2005, this jurist became just the second Italian American justice on the Supreme Court, after Antonin Scalia — who is he?
Samuel Alito: US Supreme Court justice since 2006.

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Lasting 872 days and killing an estimated 1.5 million from a prewar population of 3.2 million, this WWII blockade of the Soviet Union's second-largest city was never successfully captured — what was it?
Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.

Daughter of Darius III of Persia, she was captured after her father's defeat at Issus and became the second bride of the Macedonian conqueror at the Susa weddings in 324 BC, before being killed by his other spouse, Roxana — who was she?
Stateira (wife of Alexander the Great): Daughter of Darius III, died 323 BC.
A Thai Chinese general, he became the only king of Thonburi after leading the liberation of Siam from Burmese occupation and reuniting a country splintered among warlords — who was he?
Taksin: King of Siam from 1767 to 1782.

A protégé of Robert Walpole, this Whig statesman served as a Secretary of State for 30 unbroken years and dominated British foreign policy — and was twice Prime Minister. By which dukedom is he commonly known?
Thomas Pelham-Holles, 1st Duke of Newcastle: Prime Minister of Great Britain (1754–1756; 1757–1762)
Dubbed 'the Nelson of the East' by Western reporters, this Imperial Japanese Navy admiral penned Russia's fleet into Port Arthur before a decisive 1905 victory at Tsushima — who is he?

Spanning roughly 800 to 1050 CE, this era of Norse raiding, trading, and settlement saw Scandinavians reach as far as Newfoundland, becoming the first Europeans known to set foot in North America. What period was this?
Viking Age: Period of European history (about 800–1050)

The first conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, this 1805–1806 struggle pitted Napoleon's France against an alliance of Britain, Austria, Russia, Naples, Sicily, and Sweden, and included the Battle of Trafalgar — which conflict?
War of the Third Coalition: 1805–1806 conflict during the Napoleonic Wars. The Royal Navy, however, assured its naval dominance at the Battle of Trafalgar in October 1805.
The longest-serving member of any democratic German parliament, this CDU politician served as president of the Bundestag from 2017 to 2021 — who was he?

Regarded as the fourth person to accept Islam, this former slave became the adopted son of the Prophet Muhammad and later commanded early Muslim military expeditions, including a final raid on Byzantine-held Bosra in 629 CE — who was he?
Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi: Companion and adopted son of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.

Which of these four is the oldest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is a physicist?
Max von Laue is a physicist.
Which of these four is a chemist?
Percy Lavon Julian is a chemist. Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 – April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.
What is the atomic number of Nobelium?
Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
In what year was Alexander Hamilton born?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year did Albert Einstein die?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
In what year was Calcium discovered?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Which company manufactures Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet?
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: McDonnell Douglas. The Super Hornet is in service with the armed forces of the United States, Australia, and Kuwait.
Which country is Artemy Lebedev from?
Artemy Lebedev: Russia. Artemy Andreyevich Lebedev (Russian: Артемий Андреевич Лебедев; born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Who is credited with discovering Cadmium?
Cadmium: Friedrich Stromeyer. Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
Who is credited with discovering Pigeonhole principle?

Pigeonhole principle: Johann Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet. In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item.
Who is credited with discovering Galactic Center?
Galactic Center: Harlow Shapley. The Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.
First unearthed in Montana in 1987 by a team led by Jack Horner, this horned dinosaur genus takes its name from a Greek river deity — name the genus?
Achelousaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America, about 77 to 74.8 million years ago.

This South African bulb genus tends to flower around March, earning a local nickname tied to that month, and is often confused with the Hippeastrum plants sold at Christmas under its common name — which genus?
Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Known as 'doodlebugs' for the trails they leave in sand, these insect larvae dig pits to ambush wandering ants, while the winged adults are often mistaken for dragonflies — what are they?
Antlion are a group of about 2,000 species of insect in the neuropteran family Myrmeleontidae.
Despite the name, this gold-brown-eyed black-and-white bird of Australia isn't related to its Eurasian namesake at all — it's a butcherbird cousin in its own genus. What is it?
Australian magpie (Gymnorhina tibicen) is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand, and the Fijian island of Taveuni.
What yellow-green digestive fluid is produced continuously by the liver but stored and concentrated in the gallbladder until it's needed to break down fats in the small intestine?
Bile (from Latin bilis), also known as gall, is a yellow-green fluid produced by the liver of most vertebrates that aids the digestion of lipids in the small intestine.
One of the largest, longest-lived trees in the Amazon, this species produces a fruit and shell weighing up to two kilograms, with edible seeds famed for their selenium content — what tree is it?
Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa) refers to a South American tree of the monotypic genus Bertholletia in the family Lecythidaceae as well as the tree's commercially-harvested edible seeds.
Wolves, domestic dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals all belong to this taxonomic genus, whose members are known for massive skulls, long legs, and short ears and tails. Name the genus?
Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.

A member of the poppy family found across Europe and western Asia, this herbaceous plant is nicknamed 'greater celandine' and isn't actually related to the similarly-named 'lesser celandine' — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the poppy family Papaveraceae.
Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.
This blood-feeding parasitic insect usually lives in human pubic hair and is thought to have diverged from a closely related gorilla parasite roughly 3.3 million years ago — what is it?
Crab louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
A colorless, volatile liquid (CH2Cl2) with a sweet, chloroform-like odor, it's slightly polar, mixes with many organic solvents but not water, and is widely used as a solvent — what is it?
Dichloromethane (DCM, methylene chloride, or methylene bichloride) is an organochlorine compound with the formula CH2Cl2.
Born in German Pomerania and drawn by Franz Boas into documenting Native American languages, this anthropologist became a founding giant of American linguistics — who was he?

Edward Sapir (January 26, 1884 - February 4, 1939) was an American anthropologist-linguist, and one of the most important figures in the development of the discipline of linguistics in the United States.
This recurring set of hormone-driven reproductive changes in female mammals is interrupted by 'rest' phases and pregnancy, and has a male equivalent called rut — what is it?

Estrous cycle (from Latin oestrus 'frenzy', originally from Ancient Greek (ostros) 'gadfly') is a set of recurring physiological changes induced by reproductive hormones in females of mammalian subclass Theria.
Found on sperm cells, fungal spores and countless microbes, this tail-like structure provides motility and even senses moisture in some swarming bacteria — what is it?

Flagellum (pl.: flagella) (Latin for 'whip' or 'scourge') is a hair-like appendage that protrudes from certain plant and animal sperm cells, from fungal spores (zoospores), and from a wide range of microorganisms to provide motility.

A Belgian-British emigrant to New York, this inventor struck gold during a 1906 stay in Central America by perfecting an early instant-coffee process and building a company to mass-produce it — who was he?
George Washington (inventor) (May 20, 1871 - March 29, 1946) was a Belgian-British inventor and businessman.

Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, this non-cancerous condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men and can occur in newborns, adolescents, and older or obese men — name the condition?

Gynecomastia (also spelled gynaecomastia) is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens.
With species ranging from evergreen trees to climbing shrubs across the tropics and temperate zones, this genus's most iconic species decorates Christmas cards worldwide — what genus is it?
Holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.
More than 20 types make up this genetic skin condition, whose Greek-derived name means "fish" — a nod to its hallmark dry, thickened, scaly texture — which disorder?
Ichthyosis is a family of genetic skin disorders characterized by dry, thickened, scaly skin.
This NASA astronaut and Marine Corps test pilot commanded the SpaceX Crew-7 mission and served as a flight engineer aboard the International Space Station — who is she?
Jasmin Moghbeli (born June 24, 1983) is an American U.S.

This American game show host and former software engineer won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004, the longest streak in its history, before becoming its host himself in 2021 — who is he?
Ken Jennings (born May 23, 1974) is an American game show host and author who has hosted the syndicated quiz show Jeopardy!
Distinguished from its cousins the pikas by short furry tails and elongated ears and hind legs, this mammal family comprises over 70 species we commonly call rabbits and hares — which family?
Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
This German physicist gave aerodynamics its rigorous mathematical footing, identifying the boundary layer and lifting-line theory — and a dimensionless number bears his name. Who was he?
Ludwig Prandtl (German; 4 February 1875 - 15 August 1953) was a German fluid dynamicist, physicist and aerospace scientist.
Often called the 'father of the handheld cell phone,' this Motorola engineer placed the first public mobile call in 1973 from a New York City sidewalk — who is he?
Martin Cooper (inventor) (born December 26, 1928) is an American engineer.
Built primarily from stainless steel, this Soviet supersonic interceptor could exceed Mach 3.2, but doing so risked wrecking its own engines. What aircraft is it?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 (NATO reporting name: Foxbat) is a supersonic interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft that is among the fastest military aircraft to enter service.

This symbiotic relationship between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal threads interconnect with plant roots at the cellular level, plays a major role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — what is it called?

Born in New York to Jewish Holocaust-survivor parents, this Princeton-trained political scientist studies the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — and his 2007 DePaul tenure fight made headlines. Who is he?
Norman Finkelstein (born December 8, 1953) is an American political scientist and activist.
Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the cycle, this event sees an ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg ready to be fertilized. What's the term?
Ovulation is an important part of the menstrual cycle in female vertebrates where the egg cells are released from the ovaries as part of the ovarian cycle.
What medical term describes damage or disease affecting the nerves — impairing sensation, movement, gland, or organ function — commonly caused by systemic diseases such as diabetes?

Peripheral neuropathy is damage or disease affecting the nerves. Peripheral neuropathy may be acute (with sudden onset, rapid progress) or chronic (symptoms begin subtly and progress slowly), and may be reversible or permanent.
A member of the cashew family and a priority tree-nut allergen, this green seed saw the US, Iran, and Turkey produce 87% of the world's 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — what is it?
Pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.

This endogenous steroid sex hormone plays a central role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development, and also serves as a key metabolic intermediate for producing other steroid hormones — name the hormone?
Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
Bitter-tasting and rich in vitamin K, this Mediterranean vegetable with edible buds resembling broccoli is also known as broccoli rabe — what is it?
Rapini (broccoli rabe or raab; RAHB) is a green cruciferous vegetable, with the leaves, buds, and stems all being edible; the buds somewhat resemble broccoli.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrographs, this virus is the leading cause of diarrheal disease in infants worldwide, spread via the fecal-oral route — what is it?
Rotavirus are the most common cause of diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children.
Which chemical element, symbol Se, was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named for the moon, in a nod to its chemical similarity to tellurium, named for the Earth?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
This alkaline compound, commonly diluted in water and sold as household bleach, is derived from hypochlorous acid and is unstable in its pure anhydrous form. What is it?
Sodium hypochlorite is an alkaline inorganic chemical compound with the formula NaOCl (also written as NaClO).
A Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist who co-founded New Left Review, this thinker became a founding figure of the Birmingham School of Cultural Studies — who was he?
Stuart Hall (cultural theorist) (3 February 1932 - 10 February 2014) was a Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist, cultural theorist, and political activist.

This family of marine and freshwater fish can inflate themselves dramatically, revealing thin spines that stay hidden against their skin until they puff up — unlike their spinier, porcupine-like relatives — name this fish family?
Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.
Usually caused by mutations in the TCOF1 gene, which autosomal dominant condition affects facial bone and ear development but not intelligence?
Treacher Collins syndrome (TCS) is a genetic disorder characterized by deformities of the ears, eyes, cheekbones, and chin.
Regarded as the 'Father of the Indian space program,' this physicist and astronomer also helped develop nuclear power in India, earning the Padma Vibhushan posthumously — who is he?
Vikram Sarabhai (12 August 1919 - 30 December 1971) was an Indian physicist and astronomer who initiated space research and helped to develop nuclear power in India.

This unit of time is based on how long Earth takes to complete one full orbit around the Sun, with the precise scientific definition running about 365 days, 5 hours, and 48 minutes — what unit is this?

Year is a unit of time based on how long it takes the Earth to orbit the Sun. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Ranging from a racing tachycardia to a sluggish bradycardia, this catch-all term covers any heartbeat that strays from normal sinus rhythm — what is it called?
Arrhythmia: Group of medical conditions characterized by irregular heartbeat.
This slender projection of a nerve cell typically carries electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands — what is it called?
Axon: Long projection on a neuron that conducts signals to other neurons.
Sold under the brand name Tessalon, this cough-relief medication works within about 20 minutes by acting as a local anesthetic that blocks stretch receptors in the lungs — what is this drug called?
Benzonatate: Oral cough medication. Benzonatate, sold under the brand name Tessalon among others, is a medication that is used for the symptomatic relief of cough.
Native to tropical South America, this large non-venomous member of family Boidae is a fixture of private collections thanks to its wildly variable color patterns — what species is it?

After resigning from Evergreen State College following 2017 protests over campus racial equity, this podcaster and former evolutionary biology professor was named part of the 'intellectual dark web' — who is he?
Bret Weinstein: American podcaster and author (born 1969)
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.
Native to the Mediterranean, this legume tree's seed pods are ground into a chocolate substitute, while its seeds yield a common food thickener known as locust bean gum — which tree?
Carob: Small tree grown for its edible pods and landscaping.
This goat-antelope roams mountain ranges from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus and has even been introduced to New Zealand's South Island — which animal?
Named from Latin words meaning 'around' and 'day,' this roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle appears independently across animals, plants, fungi, and cyanobacteria?
Circadian rhythm: Natural internal process that regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?
Unlike its rocky, mountain-dwelling marmot relatives, this solitary lowland rodent — also called the woodchuck — is common across the Eastern U.S., Canada, and Alaska. What is it?
Groundhog: Species of rodent. The groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.

Often defined as the normal functioning of the body free of disease, pain, or injury, this multidimensional state of well-being can be promoted by exercise and sleep and harmed by smoking or stress — what's the one-word concept?
Health: Desirable level of functional or metabolic efficiency of a living being.
Named for the English physician who first described it in 1832, this cancer is defined by multinucleated Reed–Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes — what is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma: Type of blood and immune-system cancer.
This immune response causes tissue damage upon repeated exposure to an antigen and underlies conditions like hay fever, which affects roughly one in ten people worldwide — what is it called?
Hypersensitivity: Overreaction of the immune system to an antigen.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?
Biosynthesized in the body from the amino acid tyrosine, this compound is the direct precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — what is it?
L-DOPA: Chemical compound. As is true for many molecules, the human body produces only one of these isomers (the l-DOPA form).

Elon Musk's praise for his MIT driver-attention study on Tesla's autopilot brought this computer scientist to prominence in 2019, ahead of a career hosting long-form interviews with notable figures — who is he?
Lex Fridman: American scientist and podcast host (born 1983)
Sold under the brand name Cozaar, this angiotensin receptor blocker treats high blood pressure while also protecting the kidneys in diabetic patients — what drug is it?
Losartan: Blood pressure medication. Losartan, sold under the brand name Cozaar among others, is a medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
This theoretical physicist and science communicator bridged science and science fiction well enough to win a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for Arthur C. Clarke — who is he?
Michio Kaku: American theoretical physicist, futurist and author.

Thought to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' and a reduced risk of inbreeding-linked health problems, this catch-all term covers roughly 150 million dogs worldwide that don't belong to any officially recognized breed — what's it called?
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
This synthetic element 113 was claimed by both a Russian-American team at Dubna and, in 2004, a Japanese team at Riken. What's its name?
Nihonium: Chemical element with atomic number 113 (Nh)

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Derived from Greek words meaning 'healer of children,' this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — what is it?
Pediatrics: Branch of medicine caring for children. Within the Commonwealth, pediatrics covers patients until the age of 18, except in India where the pediatric age is 12.
Formed by stripping three protons from phosphoric acid, this triply-charged ion carries the formula PO4³⁻ and lends its name to esters like trimethyl ester in organic chemistry — what anion is it?
Phosphate: Anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Named partly for Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless aircraft, which genus of enormous azhdarchid pterosaur is a top candidate for the largest flying animal ever?
Quetzalcoatlus: Genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.

Marked by tea-colored urine and triggered by crush injuries or extreme exertion, this condition involves skeletal muscle breaking down so fast that released myoglobin can damage the kidneys — what is it called?
Rhabdomyolysis: Condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
This German engineer invented a fuel-efficient combustion engine so influential that both it and the fuel it burns bear his name — who was he?
Rudolf Diesel: German inventor and engineer (1858–1913)
About 90% of cases trace to a herniated spinal disc pressing on a nerve root, producing a shooting pain that runs from the lower back down one leg — what's the condition?
Sciatica: Lower-back pain that can extend down the leg.
Native to East Asia, this cultivated mushroom is also known as the black mushroom or Chinese mushroom — name the fungus?
About how long ago did the gravitationally bound system of the Sun and its eight planets form?
The Solar System is the gravitationally bound system of the Sun and the masses orbiting it, including its eight planets. It formed about 4.6 billion years ago.
Known by the Reddit username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded the platform and also launched the now-defunct airfare search engine Hipmunk — who is he?
Steve Huffman: American web developer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Also called the Java plum, this fast-growing evergreen tree from the Indian subcontinent can top 30 meters and live for over a century — which tree?
Syzygium cumini: Species of tree. It can reach heights of up to 30 m (100 ft) and can live more than 100 years.
Found in pufferfish, blue-ringed octopuses, and rough-skinned newts, this potent sodium-channel-blocking neurotoxin is also being trialed as a treatment for cancer-related pain — what is it?
Tetrodotoxin: Neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Nocturnal and tree-dwelling, this lizard species is native to Asia and various Pacific Islands — which reptile is it?
Tokay gecko: Species of reptile. The tokay gecko (Gekko gecko) is a nocturnal arboreal gecko in the genus Gekko, the true geckos.
Carrying the NATO nickname 'Backfire,' this supersonic Soviet bomber with variable-sweep wings first dropped conventional bombs during the Soviet–Afghan War — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22M: Russian long-range supersonic strategic bomber.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.
First isolated in 1669 by alchemist Henning Brand, this waxy, translucent form of an element glows faintly green in the dark and ignites spontaneously in air — which substance?
Sold under the brand name Ambien, which nonbenzodiazepine 'Z-drug' cuts the time to fall asleep by about fifteen minutes?
The symbol for scandium is Sc. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
